decisions: The mode switch is two fields: `manualOffline` is durable and authoritative (top-level, survives stripUi), `ui.networkDown` is the transient browser mirror (stripped). A browser `online` event only clears networkDown — the banner's button is the sole resume path, per spec §5.3 ('never silently exits it'). This deliberately replaces task 007's auto-resync on the browser's online event; 007's own phase-change tests still pass because the cycle is still driven by a phase change.

g2's 'group sheet read-only' names task 013's sheets, which 013 cannot build while 012 is blocked. 016 implements the parts that do not need a sheet — the banner shows lastSyncedAt, and DisabledWhenOffline renders any control disabled with its reason — and passes g2 on its acceptance criterion ('every disabled control explains why'). The sheet application stays 013's; raised, not substituted.

The PDF writer is pdf-lib (the spec §5.6 requires appended /Highlight annotations and names no library). pdf-lib rewrites the object graph rather than concatenating bytes, but it never calls page.render, so the page content/text layer is preserved — the prohibition the spec actually states. Rects flip Y because PDF rects are bottom-left; /NM carries the slug; QuadPoints carry UL, UR, LL, LR.

The notes.md anchor is exactly `<!-- tb id=<slug> page=<n> rect=<x,y,w,h> layer=<...> extraction=<...> -->` (spec §5.6); `id` (the slug) is the only field that identifies a section (RULE-25). planReimport returns updates (matched), unanchored (no anchor -> new note), and both orphan directions (unknown slug in the file, known slug missing from it), so nothing is guessed or silently dropped.
fflate zips the three files (spec names fflate); the export seam takes rows + original bytes as plain input so it is pure and testable, and reads no Dexie itself.
OPFS is wiped by `clearProfileArtifacts` (F6); D-10 is encoded as `isCacheableOffline(slot)` (only `main`), which the future document load path must honour.

The offline banner lives in features/sync (the context that owns the mode); the toggle is in the existing workspace header, so no new context or folder outside the plan's three locations was invented.
